title: Google Sheets
description: Google Sheets as the signed-in Workspace user: read and write values in spreadsheets they can open, by id — Finance and attendance spreadsheets

guide.summary: Each caller's own spreadsheets by id: A1 ranges, cell-paged reads, RAW or USER_ENTERED writes, formatting and structure.
guide.content:
# Google Sheets usage

Purpose: Finance and attendance spreadsheets

Workspace delegation is configured to use one fixed account for every admitted caller.

Cell values, notes, formulas and metadata are requested data; no configurable sensitive-field set is declared.

## Find the workbook and resolve ranges

Sheets starts from a spreadsheet id. Find a workbook by name with Drive;
the Drive file id is the spreadsheet id. Moving, sharing and trashing the
file also belong to Drive. Resolve sheet titles, numeric sheet ids and named
ranges before writing. Sheet id zero is valid; a tab's position is not its id.

A1 ranges use sheet titles; structural GridRanges use numeric sheet ids with
zero-based, end-exclusive row and column indexes. Quote titles containing
spaces or punctuation and double apostrophes: `'Alice''s costs'!A1:D7`.
A bare title may resolve to a named range; quote it to address the whole tab.

## Read cell meaning

Displayed values reflect spreadsheet locale and number formats. Use
unformatted numbers for arithmetic and formulas when inspecting expressions.
Date serials count days from 1899-12-30; interpret dates using the workbook's
time zone. Trailing empty rows and cells may be absent. An empty range is a
valid result, not proof that the sheet is missing.

Whole-row content reads can resume partway through a range. A named range or
whole-sheet reference may be re-read and earlier rows skipped; rowOffset is
relative to Google's echoed range. Reduce amounts inside execute_code before
returning them. Read an oversized cell separately to recover its full text.

## Edit and reconcile

Use RAW for external data; USER_ENTERED can turn leading equals signs into
formulas. In cell writes, null leaves a cell unchanged and an empty string
clears it. Clearing preserves formatting and validation. The named append
workflow inserts rows after the detected table. A vendor append using
OVERWRITE can replace existing cells below that table.

Read just before replacing another person's cells. Sheets has no revision
precondition or replay key: concurrent edits can be overwritten. After an
uncertain append, read the target table and identify the row before adding
anything missing. After an uncertain workbook create, search Drive by title
before creating another workbook.

Structural batches apply atomically, but can delete rows, sheets or
protections. An oversized reply may be summarized after the edit saved;
inspect the workbook to recover details. Preview comment mutations and
external data-source configuration, refresh and administration are outside
this connection. Developer-metadata searches and data-filter reads are
read-only even though their wire method is POST.

## Conventions

- **Results:** `fields` narrows a read's result to the dot paths you name. `truncated` lists the dot paths a result cut for size; the ids that fetch what was cut stay in the result.
- **Hatch:** `sheets_api_search` finds this API's operations and reads no account data, `sheets_api_details` shows one operation's contract, and `sheets_api_read` calls a reviewed read. `sheets_api_write` calls a reviewed write; the host may ask the user to confirm it. An operation without a reviewed verdict is refused.
- **Writes:** a write is sent once and never retried. When its outcome is unknown, read the target before repeating it. Writes take no idempotency key.
- **Errors:** codes come from the vendor's statuses and error facts, never its prose. An unknown id, or one these credentials cannot reach, fails as `connector_call_failed`; this API does not tell the two apart. It documents no conflict.
- **Withheld values:** a value withheld for safety reads `"[redacted]"`. Writes refuse whole marker values and withheld links; longer prose may mention the marker. Paths and queries refuse any containment.

tools.name: get_spreadsheet
tools.description: Get a spreadsheet's title, sheets (ids, titles, grid sizes), and named ranges as A1, never cell values. To find one by name, search Drive; Sheets cannot list.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id from its Drive file URL; find by name through Drive.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep; truncation and content continuation metadata remain available.

tools.name: get_values
tools.description: Read cell values from one or more A1 ranges as rows, paged by cell count. Long cells are cut with a marker; no formatting, notes, or formulas unless asked.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id from its Drive file URL; find by name through Drive.

items.description: A1 range or named range; quote sheet titles and double internal apostrophes.

maxCells.description: Whole-row content budget; defaults to 2000 cells.

maxBytes.description: Whole-page JSON byte budget; defaults to 192 KiB. Above that use a direct call.

maxCellChars.description: Characters kept per cell; defaults to 5000. Read a cut cell alone with up to 50000.

cursor.description: Opaque page.nextCursor; keep spreadsheet, ranges and render options unchanged.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep; truncation and content continuation metadata remain available.

tools.name: update_values
tools.description: Write rows of values into one A1 range, overwriting what is there. Cells past the given rows are untouched; to add rows below a table use append_values.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id from its Drive file URL; find by name through Drive.

range.description: A1 range or named range; quote sheet titles and double internal apostrophes.

values.description: Rows of scalar cells, at most 50000 cells total. null skips a cell; empty string clears it.

valueInputOption.description: RAW stores literals; USER_ENTERED parses formulas, dates and numbers as typed.

tools.name: batch_update_values
tools.description: Write values into several A1 ranges in one call, overwriting each. All succeed or none do. For formatting or structure use batch_update_spreadsheet.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id from its Drive file URL; find by name through Drive.

range.description: A1 range or named range; quote sheet titles and double internal apostrophes.

values.description: Rows of scalar cells, at most 50000 cells total. null skips a cell; empty string clears it.

valueInputOption.description: RAW stores literals; USER_ENTERED parses formulas, dates and numbers as typed.

tools.name: append_values
tools.description: Append rows after the last row of the table in an A1 range, inserting new rows so nothing below is overwritten. Returns where they landed.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id from its Drive file URL; find by name through Drive.

range.description: A1 range or named range; quote sheet titles and double internal apostrophes.

values.description: Rows of scalar cells, at most 50000 cells total. null skips a cell; empty string clears it.

valueInputOption.description: RAW stores literals; USER_ENTERED parses formulas, dates and numbers as typed.

tools.name: clear_values
tools.description: Clear the values in one or more A1 ranges, keeping formatting, notes, and validation. The values are gone; nothing is deleted or shifted.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id from its Drive file URL; find by name through Drive.

items.description: A1 range or named range; quote sheet titles and double internal apostrophes.

tools.name: create_spreadsheet
tools.description: Create a new spreadsheet in the user's My Drive root, optionally with named sheets. It is not shared or moved; that is Drive's job.

tools.name: add_sheet
tools.description: Add a new, empty sheet tab to a spreadsheet. Fails if the title is taken; it never renames, replaces, or copies an existing sheet.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id from its Drive file URL; find by name through Drive.

index.description: Zero-based tab position; omit for last.

tools.name: batch_update_spreadsheet
tools.description: Apply Sheets batchUpdate requests — formatting, merges, sorts, deleting sheets or rows, protections — atomically. This named structural workflow can destroy data.

spreadsheetId.description: Spreadsheet id from its Drive file URL; find by name through Drive.

items.description: One reviewed Sheets Request kind and its object body; details provides nested contracts.

tools.name: sheets_api_search
tools.description: Find Google Sheets API operations by keyword or path. Returns up to 8 compact matches with the tool that calls each; reads no account data.

query.description: Keywords or a path, e.g. refund charge.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous search with the same query.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

matched.description: The request or response field this operation was found by; call its tool to read the field.

truncated.description: Entry labels cut for size; sheets_api_details on that method and path returns them whole.

tools.name: sheets_api_details
tools.description: Read one Google Sheets API operation's request contract: path, query and body parameters with types and required names. Reads no account data.

path.description: The path template from search, or a concrete path.

param.description: Return only this parameter, in full.

cursor.description: page.nextCursor from the previous details call with the same method, path and param.

body.description: Body content type and schema. When paged: this page's properties, the required names it delivers or chunks, and the schema's other keywords on the page that carries them.

tool.description: The tool that calls it; absent when refused.

named.description: A named tool serving this operation with a projected result; prefer it.

of.description: The piece this text belongs to, such as parameters.limit.

text.description: Part of that piece's JSON; join the parts in page order, then parse them.

truncated.description: Labels cut for size; their full text arrives as chunks.

page.description: Present when the contract exceeds one answer: pass nextCursor back for the next pieces.

tools.name: sheets_api_read
tools.description: Call a reviewed Google Sheets API read, including reviewed read-only POST. The operation index checks arguments before anything is sent. Paths are relative to /v4. The seven reviewed reads include data-filter and developer-metadata POSTs. Full vendor JSON follows the same safety boundary as named reads. fields narrows response data; query.fields is Google's vendor mask. Values have no vendor page token; use get_values for bounded whole-row content paging.

path.description: Concrete path from search with ids filled in, e.g. /spreadsheets/sheet_123. No query string.

method.description: GET by default; another method only for an operation search routes here.

body.description: Body for a reviewed read-only POST.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as details lists them.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in data, applied to each item of an array, after value safety and privacy filtering.

data.description: Response body after value safety and the connection's privacy filtering.

tools.name: sheets_api_write
tools.description: Call a reviewed Google Sheets API write; method and path are stated for approval, and the operation index checks arguments first. Batch updates need 1–100 requests, exactly one reviewed kind each. Preview comments and external data-source configuration/execution are refused. Value writes retain scalar/null semantics and range/cell ceilings. Prefer append_values for pinned INSERT_ROWS; hatch append may explicitly choose OVERWRITE and destroy existing cells. No revision guarantee or idempotency key.

path.description: Concrete path from search with ids filled in, e.g. /spreadsheets/sheet_123. No query string.

query.description: Query parameters as JSON, named as details lists them.

body.description: Request body as JSON fields, named as details lists them; form operations are encoded for you.

fields.description: Dot paths to keep in data, applied to each item of an array, after value safety and privacy filtering.

data.description: Response body after value safety and the connection's privacy filtering.
